stations.zh: 雅典藝術現場
stations.en: Athens Art Scene: Streets, Markets & Museums
stations.zhText: 抵達雅典的前四天，把城市當成一層層疊起來的書來讀：哈德良圖書館的科林斯柱廊就在莫納斯提拉基地鐵站旁，奧林匹亞宙斯神殿展現羅馬尺度的古典柱式；憲法廣場的總統衛隊交接是一場編舞，小主教座堂則把古老石雕再利用在牆上。中央市場的手寫價目卡、普西里的塗鴉與 Little Kook 主題立面，是最生動的庶民字體與沉浸式品牌。比雷埃夫斯考古博物館的青銅雅典娜、悲劇面具、幾何風格與黑繪陶瓶、棕櫚葉飾墓碑，一館看盡希臘裝飾史。也在比雷埃夫斯大學認識了學生 Stelios，在學生餐廳共進午餐。
stations.enText: These first four days in Athens (雅典) and its port, Piraeus (比雷埃夫斯), read the city as a layered palimpsest (城市層疊). Classical ruins sit inside a Neoclassical (新古典主義) capital rebuilt after 1834: the Corinthian colonnade (科林斯柱廊) of Hadrian's Library stands beside the Monastiraki metro, and the columns of the Temple of Olympian Zeus (奧林匹亞宙斯神殿) show the Roman scale of the classical orders (古典柱式). At Syntagma Square (憲法廣場) the Evzones (總統衛隊) perform a choreographed changing of the guard, while the Little Metropolis (小主教座堂) reuses carved spolia (再利用石材). Everyday design is just as instructive: handwritten price cards at the Central Market (中央市場), graffiti in Psirri (普西里) and the themed façade of Little Kook show vernacular typography (庶民字體) and immersive branding (沉浸式品牌). The Archaeological Museum of Piraeus adds monumental bronze casting (青銅鑄造), with the bronze Athena and a tragic mask, Geometric (幾何風格) and black-figure (黑繪) vases, and stelae crowned by palmettes (棕櫚葉飾): a compact history of Greek ornament in a single port museum. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from two Athenians on the street, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings. At the University of Piraeus (比雷埃夫斯大學) we met Stelios, a student there, and shared lunch with him in the university cafeteria (大學餐廳), a first friendship in Greece.

stations.zh: MSC Lirica 郵輪
stations.zhText: 郵輪本身就是一件漂浮的旅宿設計。2003 年在法國聖納澤爾建造的 MSC Lirica，把旅館、餐廳和休閒甲板塞進一個鋼鐵船身，每個空間都受船舶設計的限制。船艙示範緊湊空間規劃：內建家具、圓角和多功能檯面，適合會搖晃的環境；自助餐廳則是動線設計與食物陳列的教材。開闊的甲板把海平線本身變成主景，是郵輪體驗的核心「框景」。在比雷埃夫斯與各港口進出港時，白色上層結構與港市紋理形成對比；海上的夕陽則上了一堂自然光與色溫的課。
stations.enText: A cruise ship is a floating piece of hospitality design (旅宿設計). MSC Lirica, built in 2003 at Saint-Nazaire in France, packs a hotel, restaurants and leisure decks into a steel hull, so every space is shaped by naval architecture (船舶設計) constraints. The cabin shows compact space planning (緊湊空間規劃): built-in furniture, rounded edges and multi-purpose surfaces that suit a moving environment. The buffet is a study in circulation design (動線設計) and food display, with serving stations arranged for large numbers of passengers at once. The deck whirlpool and open decks turn the horizon itself into the main view, a framing device (框景) that is the core of the cruise experience. Arrival and departure scenes at Piraeus and other ports show the ship as an object in the cityscape, its white superstructure (上層結構) contrasting with the dense harbour fabric. Sunsets at sea give a lesson in natural light and colour temperature (色溫). Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from the ship's crew, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 以弗所
stations.zhText: 以弗所是羅馬東方保存最完整的城市之一（世界遺產）。沿著庫瑞忒斯大道往下走，盡頭就是塞爾蘇斯圖書館，示範羅馬城市設計的「端景」手法。圖書館立面是兩層成對柱與壁龕框架組成的屏幕，刻滿科林斯柱頭與渦卷紋；哈德良神廟在柱頂楣構中間拱起一道「敘利亞拱」，是羅馬人對希臘神廟正面的變奏。山坡宅邸保存了幾何馬賽克地板與壁畫殘片。站在圖書館前的人像照，最能看出立面的尺度。
stations.enText: Ephesus (以弗所) is one of the best-preserved cities of the Roman East and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walking down Curetes Street (庫瑞忒斯大道) toward the Library of Celsus (塞爾蘇斯圖書館) shows Roman urban design (羅馬城市設計): a paved, sloping street lined with fountains and monuments that ends in a framed vista (端景). The library façade, built in the early second century AD, is a two-storey screen of paired columns and aediculae (壁龕框架), richly carved with Corinthian capitals (科林斯柱頭) and scroll ornament (渦卷紋). On the Temple of Hadrian (哈德良神廟), an arch springs from the entablature (柱頂楣構) between columns, a typically Roman variation on the Greek temple front. In the Terrace Houses (山坡宅邸), wealthy homes preserve floor mosaics (馬賽克地板) in geometric patterns and fragments of wall painting (壁畫). Together they show how Roman builders combined classical orders, ornament and engineering into theatrical urban scenery. The scale of the library façade is best understood with a person standing in front of it, which the photographs here allow.

stations.zh: 伊斯坦堡藍色清真寺與大巴扎
stations.zhText: 藍色清真寺（蘇丹艾哈邁德清真寺，1609–1616）是古典鄂圖曼建築晚期的傑作：中央圓頂坐在帆拱上，四個半圓頂層層撐開，形成向中心聚攏的空間，由四根巨柱承重。室內因數千片伊茲尼克磁磚與彩繪的藍色調而得名；外面的中庭被圓頂拱廊環繞，六座宣禮塔勾勒天際線。旁邊的賽馬場保留了狄奧多西方尖碑。大巴扎是世界最古老的室內市集之一，拱頂街道組織起陶瓷、甜點與玻璃店鋪，是活生生的工藝陳列展；廣場上的小攤車則替宏偉的場景加上日常設計的人性尺度。
stations.enText: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque (蘇丹艾哈邁德清真寺), known as the Blue Mosque, was built in 1609–1616 by the architect Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa and is a late masterpiece of classical Ottoman architecture (鄂圖曼建築). Its central dome rests on pendentives (帆拱) and is buttressed by four semi-domes (半圓頂), creating a cascading, centralised space; four massive piers (巨柱) carry the load. The interior takes its popular name from the blue tones of thousands of İznik tiles (伊茲尼克磁磚) and painted decoration. Outside, the courtyard is ringed by a domed arcade (拱廊), and six minarets (宣禮塔) mark the skyline. The adjacent Hippodrome keeps the Egyptian Obelisk of Theodosius (方尖碑), re-erected in the fourth century. In the Grand Bazaar (大巴扎), one of the oldest covered markets in the world, vaulted streets (拱頂街道) organise shops selling ceramics, sweets and glass, a living showcase of craft display. Small details, such as a street vendor's cart in Sultanahmet Square, add the human scale of everyday design to the monumental setting. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a bazaar shopkeeper, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 科孚島
stations.zhText: 科孚島受威尼斯統治約四百年，老城（世界遺產）至今仍是一座威尼斯式城市：綠色百葉窗的高窄建築夾著稱為 kantounia 的小巷，部分街道以拱廊提供遮蔭與連續店面。聖斯皮里頓教堂的天花板以鍍金框分格、嵌入彩繪板，是東正教聖像與西方巴洛克框飾混合的藻井式天花。威尼斯式鐘樓、清楚易讀的希臘文街名牌是公共字體的小課題。出城到帕萊奧卡斯特里察，石灰岩海岬、海灣與碧綠海水構成島嶼的地景；粉彩灰泥、百葉窗與鍛鐵陽台則組成老城統一的色彩計畫。
stations.enText: Corfu (科孚島) was ruled by Venice for about four centuries, and its Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, still reads as a Venetian city (威尼斯式城市). Tall, narrow buildings with green shutters line narrow lanes called kantounia (小巷), and some streets are lined with arcades (拱廊) that give shade and continuous shopfronts. Inside the Church of Saint Spyridon (聖斯皮里頓教堂), the ceiling is divided into gilded frames holding painted panels, a coffered ceiling (藻井式天花) that mixes Orthodox iconography with Western Baroque (巴洛克) framing; gold-framed icons (聖像畫) continue the theme. A church with a Venetian-style campanile (鐘樓) shows the same cross-cultural mix in the skyline. Street name signs in Greek with clear lettering are a small study in civic typography (公共字體). Outside town, the coast at Paleokastritsa (帕萊奧卡斯特里察) shows the landscape setting of the island: limestone headlands, coves and turquoise water. Pastel plaster, shutters and wrought-iron balconies give the Old Town its unified colour palette (色彩計畫).

stations.zh: 阿爾貝羅貝洛蘑菇屋與巴里
stations.zhText: 阿爾貝羅貝洛的蘑菇屋（Trulli，世界遺產）是風土建築的經典：不用灰漿的乾砌石構造，厚厚的石灰白牆上，用石灰岩片一圈圈向內疊澀收成圓錐屋頂，頂端再加上雕刻尖飾。屋頂上用白灰畫的宗教、星象與護身符號，像一套民間的符號系統。從高處看，成群的圓錐屋頂形成近乎模組化的聚落。下午到巴里，舊城窄巷、仿羅馬式鐘樓與巴洛克教堂立面，呈現南義另一種石、光與裝飾的城市傳統。
stations.enText: The trulli (蘑菇屋) of Alberobello (阿爾貝羅貝洛), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are a striking case of vernacular architecture (風土建築). They are built by dry-stone construction (乾砌石構造), without mortar: thick whitewashed (石灰粉刷) walls carry conical roofs made of corbelled (疊澀) limestone slabs, each ring stepping slightly inward until the cone closes. A carved pinnacle (屋頂尖飾) often crowns the top, and many roofs carry symbols painted in white lime, religious, astrological or protective signs that work like a vernacular sign system (符號系統); an information board explains their meanings. Seen from above, the clustered cones form a repetitive, almost modular townscape (模組化聚落). The trullo form is also used in larger buildings, as the church interior shows. In the afternoon in Bari (巴里), the narrow lanes of the old town and a Baroque (巴洛克) church façade show a contrasting southern Italian urban tradition of stone, light and ornament. The trulli show how local material, climate and construction method together produce a strong regional identity.

stations.zh: 古希臘考古與衛城
stations.en: Ancient Greece: National Archaeological Museum & Acropolis
stations.zhText: 兩天從器物一路看到紀念建築。國家考古博物館涵蓋史前到羅馬時期的希臘設計：錘揲的邁錫尼金飾、抽象的基克拉澤斯人偶、阿克羅蒂里的濕壁畫、紅繪陶器，以及青銅阿提米西昂騎師像。衛城上的帕德嫩神殿定義了多立克柱式，以柱身收分曲線（卷殺）與細微弧度，讓建築看起來筆直又有生命；伊瑞克提翁神殿則以纖細的愛奧尼柱式與女像柱門廊回應。山下是戴奧尼索斯劇場與新衛城博物館，鷹架提醒我們：文物保存是持續進行的設計工作。小器物與大建築共用同一套比例與裝飾語言。
stations.enText: Two days trace classical Greece from object to monument. The National Archaeological Museum (國家考古博物館) surveys Greek design from prehistory to the Roman period: Mycenaean gold (邁錫尼金飾) in repoussé (錘揲), abstract Cycladic figurines (基克拉澤斯人偶), fresco (濕壁畫) paintings from Akrotiri, red-figure (紅繪) pottery and the bronze Jockey of Artemision (阿提米西翁騎師). On the Acropolis (雅典衛城), the Parthenon (帕德嫩神殿) defines the Doric order (多立克柱式), refined by entasis (柱身收分曲線) and subtle curves so that it looks straight and alive. The Erechtheion (伊瑞克提翁神殿) answers with the slender Ionic order (愛奧尼柱式) and its Porch of the Caryatids (女像柱). Below the hill lie the Theatre of Dionysus and the new Acropolis Museum, while scaffolding reminds us that conservation (文物保存) is a continuous design task. Together the museum and the hill show how small crafted objects and great buildings share one language of proportion and ornament. Over lunch, a chat with a local diner who works at the city's water utility (自來水公司) offered a glimpse of everyday Athens beyond the monuments.

stations.zh: 雅典博物館與新古典城市
stations.zhText: 三天從博物館走到城市街道。屈米設計的衛城博物館（2009）浮在考古遺址上，有玻璃地板，頂樓的帕德嫩展廳與神殿對齊。拜占庭與基督教博物館展出玻璃鑲嵌片馬賽克、金底聖像與雕刻聖像屏；貝納基博物館從古代金工一路到民間刺繡與各地服飾。大學路上的漢森兄弟「新古典三部曲」以古典柱式與彩飾替新生的希臘國家建立形象。附近鐵與玻璃構成的中央市場示範功能性陳列與手寫字，普拉卡的小教堂則可看到磚框石砌法。館藏與城市合起來，講的是從大理石紀念物到無名日常工藝的同一個希臘設計故事。
stations.enText: Three days move from museum galleries to the streets that frame them. Bernard Tschumi's Acropolis Museum (衛城博物館, 2009) floats above an excavation, with glass floors (玻璃地板) and a top-floor Parthenon Gallery aligned with the temple. The Byzantine and Christian Museum (拜占庭與基督教博物館) shows mosaics of glass tesserae (鑲嵌片), gold-ground icons (聖像畫) and a carved iconostasis (聖像屏), and the Benaki Museum (貝納基博物館) runs from ancient goldwork (金工) to folk embroidery (刺繡織品) and regional costumes. On Panepistimiou Street, the Hansen brothers' Neoclassical Trilogy (新古典三部曲) used the classical orders and polychromy (彩飾) to give the new Greek state an identity. Nearby, the iron and glass (鐵與玻璃) Central Market (中央市場) shows functional display and hand-lettering (手寫字), and the small churches of Plaka (普拉卡) show cloisonné masonry (磚框石砌法). Collections and city together tell one continuous story of Greek design, from monumental marble to anonymous everyday craft. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a shared plate of food on the street, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 阿提卡與德爾菲聖地
stations.en: Attica & Delphi: Daphni, Sounion, Philopappos & Delphi
stations.zhText: 四天探索神聖建築與地景的關係。達夫尼修道院（世界遺產）的八角圓頂教堂，有約 1100 年的金底馬賽克，呈現沉靜、帶古典氣息的中期拜占庭藝術。海岸邊的武里亞格梅尼湖是喀斯特地景；蘇尼恩角的多立克式波賽頓神廟，選址讓航海者遠遠就能看見，也替海平線取景。雅典菲洛帕波斯山上有羅馬紀念墓碑，皮基奧尼斯設計的石徑把人引向衛城的框景。德爾菲的阿波羅聖域以台地式嵌進帕納索斯山，有多邊形砌石牆、雅典人寶庫與青銅御者像。選址、動線與視野和建築本身一樣重要。
stations.enText: Four days explore how sacred buildings relate to landscape. Daphni Monastery (達夫尼修道院), a UNESCO site, has an octagon-domed church whose gold-ground mosaics (金底馬賽克) of around 1100 show calm, classicising Middle Byzantine (中期拜占庭) art. On the coast, Lake Vouliagmeni (武里亞格梅尼湖) shows a karst (喀斯特) landscape, and at Cape Sounion (蘇尼恩角) the Doric Temple of Poseidon (波賽頓神廟) is sited (選址) to be seen by sailors and to frame the horizon. In Athens, Philopappos Hill (菲洛帕波斯山) carries a Roman funerary monument (紀念墓碑), and Dimitris Pikionis's stone paths (景觀建築) guide walkers to framed views (框景) of the Acropolis. At Delphi (德爾菲), the sanctuary of Apollo is terraced (台地式) into Mount Parnassus, with a polygonal masonry (多邊形砌石) wall, the Athenian Treasury and the bronze Charioteer (德爾菲御者). In every case, siting, approach and view are as important as the buildings themselves: architecture and landscape form a single composition. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from local friends, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 拉羅尼斯珠寶與梅特歐拉
stations.en: Lalaounis Jewellery & the Monasteries of Meteora
stations.zhText: 兩種尺度完全不同的設計。拉羅尼斯珠寶博物館位在衛城下方金匠的舊工坊，把古代、拜占庭與自然的元素轉譯成可以戴的形式：歷史主義遇上生物形態設計，昆蟲、鳥和蛇以黃金與彩色琺瑯呈現，金冠呼應古代葬禮花冠，手環繞著手腕，把身體當成結構。梅特歐拉（世界遺產）的東正教修道院立在卡蘭巴卡上方巨大的砂岩與礫岩石柱上，是適應極端地形的戲劇性案例；魯薩努、聖斯德望與大梅特歐拉以木陽台和木梯攀附岩壁，室內有後拜占庭濕壁畫、鍍金聖像屏與金底馬賽克。從胸針到山頂修道院，工藝都被它的所在形塑。
stations.enText: Two very different scales of design. The Ilias Lalaounis Jewelry Museum (拉羅尼斯珠寶博物館), in the goldsmith's former workshop below the Acropolis, translates ancient, Byzantine and natural sources into wearable form. Historicism (歷史主義) meets biomorphic design (生物形態設計): insects, birds and serpents are rendered in gold and coloured enamel (琺瑯), a gold wreath recalls ancient funerary wreaths, and bracelets coil around the wrist, using the body as structure. At Meteora (梅特歐拉), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Orthodox monasteries stand on huge sandstone and conglomerate (礫岩) pillars above Kalambaka, a dramatic case of architecture adapted to extreme topography (極端地形). Rousanou, St Stephen and the Great Meteoron cling to the rock with timber balconies and stairs, while inside post-Byzantine frescoes (後拜占庭濕壁畫), a gilded iconostasis (聖像屏) and a gold-ground mosaic continue sacred traditions. From a brooch to a mountain monastery, both places show craft shaped by its setting, whether wrist or rock. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from our bus driver, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 雅典市集、舊國會與主教座堂
stations.en: Athens Street Market, Old Parliament & Cathedrals
stations.zhText: 一個週末對照臨時與永久的設計。每週一次的露天市集（laiki）是臨時性建築：遮陽棚、折疊桌與箱子把普通街道變成一早上的市場，手寫價目卡與番茄、柳橙、朝鮮薊的色塊配置，是免費的招牌與陳列課。隔天到舊國會大樓裡的國家歷史博物館，看半圓形議場、浮雕銀器、各地服飾與刺繡字母樣布，是一堂早期的字體課。附近拜占庭復興式的雅典主教座堂以鍍金聖像屏為中心；小巧的中世紀小主教座堂用再利用石材砌成，古代浮雕像拼貼一樣嵌在牆上。攤位、議會、教堂，短短步行就看到三種尺度的公共設計。
stations.enText: A weekend contrasts temporary and permanent design. The laiki (露天市集), the weekly street market, is ephemeral architecture (臨時性建築): awnings, folding tables and crates turn an ordinary street into a marketplace for a morning. Handwritten price cards and colour blocking (色塊配置) of tomatoes, oranges and artichokes are a free lesson in signage and display. The next day, the National Historical Museum (國家歷史博物館) in the Neoclassical (新古典主義) Old Parliament House (舊國會大樓) keeps a semicircular debating chamber (議場), silver worked in relief (浮雕), regional costumes and an embroidered alphabet sampler (刺繡字母樣布), an early lesson in letterforms. Nearby, the Byzantine Revival (拜占庭復興式) Metropolitan Cathedral (雅典主教座堂) centres on a gilded iconostasis (聖像屏), while the tiny medieval Little Metropolis (小主教座堂) is built of spolia (再利用石材), ancient reliefs set into its walls like a collage (拼貼). Street stall, parliament and church show three scales of public design within a short walk. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a local student who cut my hair, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 伊斯坦堡：街道、拜占庭與金角灣
stations.en: Istanbul: Streets, Byzantium & the Golden Horn
stations.zhText: 四天在伊斯坦堡穿越歷史的層次。獨立大道是折衷主義建築的型錄，霓虹招牌與新哥德式的聖安東尼教堂並陳。舊城地底的地下水宮殿是 336 根柱子組成的森林，有再利用的梅杜莎頭像和劇場般的照明設計。聖索菲亞大教堂把巨大圓頂架在帆拱上，拜占庭馬賽克與伊斯蘭書法同處一室。金角灣對岸的加拉達塔與梅夫拉維道堂（旋轉舞儀式的所在），分別是城市地標與儀式空間。香料市集與卡德柯伊市場把色彩變成陳列設計；拉赫米柯曲博物館與塔沙內伊斯坦堡把船廠與鑄造廠活化為博物館和公共空間，是工業遺產再利用的範例。
stations.enText: Four days in Istanbul cross layers of history. İstiklal Avenue (獨立大道) is a catalogue of eclecticism (折衷主義) with neon signs (霓虹招牌) and the Neo-Gothic Church of St Anthony (聖安東尼教堂). Beneath the old city, the Basilica Cistern (地下水宮殿) is a forest of 336 columns, with reused Medusa heads (梅杜莎頭像) and theatrical lighting design (照明設計). Hagia Sophia (聖索菲亞大教堂) raised a vast dome on pendentives (帆拱), and its Byzantine mosaics and Ottoman calligraphy (伊斯蘭書法) coexist in one interior. Across the Golden Horn (金角灣), Galata Tower (加拉達塔) and the Mevlevi Lodge (加拉達梅夫拉維道堂), home of the whirling sema (旋轉舞儀式), show urban landmark and ritual space. The Spice Bazaar (香料市集) and Kadıköy market display colour as visual merchandising (陳列設計), while the Rahmi M. Koç Museum (拉赫米柯曲博物館) and Tersane Istanbul (塔沙內伊斯坦堡) turn shipyards and foundries into museums and public space, an example of adaptive reuse (活化再利用) of industrial heritage (工業遺產). Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from shared meals at local tables, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 華沙采風
stations.zhText: 這一週在華沙取樣城市的記憶與新生。由舊電車發電站改建的華沙起義博物館，用黑暗空間、聲音與人像牆做沉浸式展示，把歷史變成敘事空間。附近的諾布林納工廠把金屬工廠改成商店與辦公室，保留老工廠字體，是活化再利用的範本。華沙大學圖書館（1999）頂上是歐洲最大的屋頂花園之一，建築與地景融為一體。1944 年被摧毀、依照貝洛托十八世紀畫作重建的舊城，是列入世界遺產的重建案例，有刮畫立面。植物園與動物園示範解說設計（包括扎賓斯基別墅的故事），壁畫、廣告柱與重建的新世界街則展現城市的平面文化。
stations.enText: This week in Warsaw (華沙) samples the city's layers of memory and renewal. The Warsaw Rising Museum (華沙起義博物館), in a former tram power station, uses immersive exhibition design (沉浸式展示設計): dark spaces, sound and walls of portraits turn history into narrative space (敘事空間). Nearby, Fabryka Norblina (諾布林納工廠) converts a metalworks into shops and offices, a model of adaptive reuse (活化再利用) that keeps the old factory lettering. The University of Warsaw Library (華沙大學圖書館, 1999) carries one of Europe's largest roof gardens (屋頂花園), opened in 2002, where building and landscape merge. The Old Town (舊城), destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt with the help of Bernardo Bellotto's eighteenth-century paintings, is a UNESCO-listed example of reconstruction (重建) with sgraffito (刮畫) façades. The Botanic Garden and the Zoo show interpretation design (解說設計), including the story of the Żabiński Villa (扎賓斯基別墅), while murals (壁畫), poster columns (廣告柱) and the rebuilt Neoclassical street of Nowy Świat (新世界街) reveal the city's graphic culture. A one-minute video opens the folder and explains why Poland's borders moved west after 1945. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from Warsaw residents, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 卡齊米日多爾尼
stations.zhText: 卡齊米日多爾尼是維斯瓦河畔的小鎮，以波蘭文藝復興建築與長年的藝術家聚落聞名。市集廣場周圍裝飾華麗的市民住宅呈現在地的矯飾主義風格，有浮雕、壁柱與裝飾女兒牆，其中立面上有聖人像的普日貝瓦兄弟之家最有名。帶拱廊、陡斜木瓦屋頂的傳統房屋是當地風土建築木構的一面；教區教堂有文藝復興立面，鐘樓高過廣場。山坡上林間的木造別墅延續木構傳統，手繪招牌與活動海報替這個畫家小鎮加上當代的平面層次；窄巷通往穀倉，讓人想起小鎮作為河港糧食貿易地的過去。
stations.enText: Kazimierz Dolny (卡齊米日多爾尼) is a small town on the Vistula famous for its Polish Renaissance (波蘭文藝復興) architecture and as a long-time artists' colony. Around the Market Square, richly decorated burgher houses (市民住宅) show the local Mannerist (矯飾主義) style, with carved reliefs, pilasters and ornamental parapets; the Przybyła brothers' houses, with figures of saints on their façades, are the best-known example. Traditional houses with arcades (拱廊) and steep shingle roofs (木瓦屋頂) show the timber side of the region's vernacular architecture (風土建築). The parish church presents a Renaissance façade, and its bell tower rises above the square. On the hillsides, wooden villas and cottages among trees continue the timber tradition. Hand-painted signs and event posters add a contemporary graphic layer appropriate to a town of painters. Narrow lanes lead to granaries (穀倉) that recall the town's past as a grain-trading port on the river.

stations.zh: 托倫
stations.zhText: 托倫是哥白尼的故鄉，也是漢薩同盟世界保存最好的磚造哥德式城鎮之一（世界遺產）。波羅的海一帶缺乏好石材，牆、塔、教堂都用紅磚砌成，裝飾也靠磚本身完成：階梯山牆上的盲龕帶來節奏與陰影，尖拱窗裡有玫瑰紋花窗格。斜塔與城牆是沿河的防禦系統，教堂裡的彩繪玻璃與巴洛克祭壇則是後來的色彩層次。橫跨維斯瓦河的鋼桁架橋，和 Wozownia 藝廊的標誌，讓老城也看得到當代設計。
stations.enText: The medieval town of Toruń (托倫), birthplace of Nicolaus Copernicus and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is one of the best-preserved Brick Gothic (磚造哥德式) towns of the Hanseatic world. Brick Gothic developed around the Baltic, where good building stone was scarce: walls, towers and churches are built of red brick, and ornament is created through brick itself. Stepped gables (階梯山牆) are decorated with blind niches (盲龕), recessed panels that give rhythm and shadow without openings, and pointed windows are filled with tracery (花窗格) including rose motifs. The Leaning Tower (斜塔) and the city walls show the fortification system along the river. Inside churches, stained glass (彩繪玻璃) and Baroque (巴洛克) altars add colour and later layers. The Copernicus statue stands near the Town Hall. A steel truss bridge (鋼桁架橋) crosses the Vistula, and the Wozownia gallery's logo shows contemporary graphic design in the historic town.

stations.zh: 羅茲：車站、工廠與皮奧特科夫斯卡街
stations.zhText: 羅茲曾是波蘭最大的紡織城，如今是後工業城市再生的實驗室。2016 年重新啟用的羅茲法布里奇納車站把月台放到地下，上方是鋼構玻璃大廳，是基礎設施設計的範例。曼努法克圖拉把波茲南斯基的紅磚棉紡廠改成購物、休閒與博物館區，是中歐最大的活化再利用案之一，紅磚立面圍出新的公共廣場。城市主軸皮奧特科夫斯卡街兩側的公寓樓房，以折衷主義與新藝術立面、浮雕與馬賽克組成戶外的裝飾風格藝廊；青銅座椅雕塑把街道家具變成公共藝術，舊工廠 OFF Piotrkowska 則成了由下而上的創意街區。
stations.enText: Łódź (羅茲), once Poland's great textile city, is a laboratory of post-industrial regeneration. Łódź Fabryczna station (羅茲法布里奇納車站), reopened in 2016, puts its platforms underground beneath a steel-and-glass hall (鋼構玻璃大廳), an example of infrastructure design (基礎設施設計). Manufaktura (曼努法克圖拉) converts Izrael Poznański's red-brick cotton mills (紅磚工業建築) into a shopping, leisure and museum district, one of Central Europe's largest adaptive reuse (活化再利用) projects, with a new public square framed by brick façades. Piotrkowska Street (皮奧特科夫斯卡街), the city's main axis, is lined with tenement houses (公寓樓房) whose eclectic (折衷主義) and Art Nouveau (新藝術) façades, reliefs and mosaics form an outdoor gallery of decorative styles. Bronze bench sculptures (座椅雕塑) turn street furniture into public art, and OFF Piotrkowska, a former factory, has become a bottom-up creative district. In one day, the city shows two scales of reuse: large planned conversion and informal creative occupation.

stations.zh: 柯希基市場與歐洲團結中心
stations.en: Hala Koszyki & the European Solidarity Centre
stations.zhText: 華沙與格但斯克的兩棟建築，說明新設計如何承載場所記憶。柯希基市場是 1906–1908 年的新藝術市場大廳，2016 年重建為美食廳：鉚接鋼桁架與玻璃屋頂下，餐廳像小島一樣散布，各家招牌拼貼出品牌識別，是生動的活化再利用。格但斯克的歐洲團結中心（FORT Architekci，2014）就在 1980 年團結工聯誕生的船廠大門旁，以傾斜的耐候鋼板包覆，讓人想起建造中的船身，是材料象徵的範例；室內的冬季花園與運用大型字體和檔案影像的深色展廳形成對比，參觀者的手寫留言也成為設計的一部分。
stations.enText: Two buildings, in Warsaw (華沙) and Gdańsk (格但斯克), show how new design can carry the memory of a place. Hala Koszyki (柯希基市場), an Art Nouveau (新藝術) market hall of 1906–1908, was rebuilt and reopened in 2016 as a food hall: under its riveted steel trusses and glazed roof (玻璃屋頂), restaurants are set as islands, and each outlet's signage forms a collage of brand identities (品牌識別), a lively example of adaptive reuse (活化再利用). In Gdańsk, the European Solidarity Centre (歐洲團結中心) by FORT Architekci, opened in 2014 beside the shipyard gate where Solidarity was born in 1980, is clad in angled weathering steel (耐候鋼) that recalls ship hulls under construction, an example of material symbolism (材料象徵). Inside, a winter garden (室內花園) contrasts with dark exhibition halls that use large typography (大型字體) and archival images, and visitors' handwritten messages become part of the design. Both buildings turn history into a public space that people actually use every day.

stations.zh: 弗羅茨瓦夫老城與百年廳
stations.en: Wrocław: Old Town, Dwarfs & Centennial Hall
stations.zhText: 在弗羅茨瓦夫的一天，從哥德式的市民驕傲走到早期現代主義的工程。歐洲最大之一的市集廣場，周圍是山牆市民住宅，中央是有階梯山牆、尖塔與天文鐘的哥德式舊市政廳；教堂塔樓的磚造螺旋樓梯通往屋頂景觀。2005 年起散布全城的青銅小矮人，呼應反共的「橘色另類運動」，把公共藝術變成尋寶遊戲與城市品牌。市中心東邊，馬克斯．伯格設計的百年廳（1913，世界遺產）以肋狀鋼筋混凝土圓頂跨距約 65 公尺，靠一圈圈階梯狀高側窗採光；周邊珀爾齊希的四圓頂館與長長的混凝土藤架，把新材料用在景觀上。
stations.enText: A day in Wrocław (弗羅茨瓦夫) spans Gothic civic pride and early Modernist engineering. The Market Square (市集廣場), one of Europe's largest, is lined with gabled burgher houses (山牆市民住宅) and centred on the Gothic Old Town Hall (舊市政廳) with its stepped gables, pinnacles and astronomical clock. A brick spiral staircase (螺旋樓梯) leads up a church tower for a view over the roofs. All over the city, small bronze dwarfs (小矮人銅像), placed since 2005 and recalling the anti-communist Orange Alternative movement, turn public art (公共藝術) into a treasure hunt and city branding (城市品牌). East of the centre, Max Berg's Centennial Hall (百年廳, 1913), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, spans about 65 metres with a ribbed reinforced concrete (鋼筋混凝土) dome lit by stepped rings of clerestory windows (高側窗). Around it, Hans Poelzig's Four Domes Pavilion and the long concrete pergola (藤架) show the new material used for landscape. The day moves from ornament to structure as expression.

stations.zh: 格但斯克老城與波浪大樓
stations.zhText: 在格但斯克的兩天，把兩種「集體的城市」放在一起看。這座富裕的漢薩同盟港口，主城結合中世紀磚造哥德式與荷蘭影響的矯飾主義：莫特瓦河畔的起重機城門、長街與長市場、亞瑟宮，以及窄長的市民住宅，用裝飾山牆、紋章與獅面雕刻宣示商人地位。大部分在 1945 年被毀、戰後重建，新的水岸建築則重新詮釋山牆屋，是文脈設計的例子。往北幾公里，普日莫熱區的波浪大樓（1970–1973）長約 860 公尺、11 層樓、1,792 戶，以開放外廊進出，用大型預鑄構件建成，微微彎曲的波浪平面柔化了集合住宅的重複感。
stations.enText: Two days in Gdańsk (格但斯克) set two kinds of collective city side by side. The Main Town of this rich Hanseatic (漢薩同盟) port combines medieval Brick Gothic (磚造哥德式) with Dutch-influenced Mannerism (荷蘭矯飾主義): the Crane (起重機) on the Motława River, Long Street and Long Market (長市場) with Artus Court (亞瑟宮), and narrow burgher houses (市民住宅) whose decorated gables, carved coats of arms (紋章裝飾) and lion masks advertised merchant status. Most of it was destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt after the war, and new waterfront buildings now reinterpret the gabled house, an example of contextual design (文脈設計). A few kilometres north, the Falowiec (波浪大樓) in Przymorze, built in 1970–1973, is about 860 metres long and eleven storeys high, with 1,792 flats reached from open access galleries (外廊). Built from large prefabricated blocks (預鑄構件), its gently bent, wave-like plan softens the repetition of mass housing (集合住宅). Both are long, rhythmic street walls: one assembled plot by plot over centuries, the other in four years as a single industrial object. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a young local, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 馬爾堡城堡
stations.zhText: 馬爾堡城堡由條頓騎士團自十三世紀末興建，是全世界面積最大的磚造城堡，也是世界遺產，更是磚造哥德式的傑作：上、中、下三座城堡以護城河、城門、吊橋與塔樓串連，全部是紅磚。室內的拱頂是重點：大食堂裡纖細的柱子撐起棕櫚拱頂，肋骨像棕櫚葉一樣從單一支點散開，形成輕盈開闊的大廳；其他房間則有肋拱與彩繪牆面，另有木天花板大廳展示不同的結構手法。雕刻的哥德式大門與彩繪玻璃展現細緻工藝，琥珀收藏則讓人想起讓騎士團致富的波羅的海貿易。城堡在 1945 年嚴重受損，經過數十年修復。
stations.enText: Malbork Castle (馬爾堡城堡), built by the Teutonic Order (條頓騎士團) from the late thirteenth century, is the largest brick castle in the world by area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is a masterpiece of Brick Gothic (磚造哥德式): the High, Middle and Lower Castles are linked by moats, gates, drawbridges and towers, all in red brick. Inside, the vaults are the highlight. In the Grand Refectory, slender columns carry palm vaults (棕櫚拱頂), where ribs spread from a single support like the fronds of a palm, creating a light, open hall; in other rooms rib vaults (肋拱) rise above painted walls. A hall with a wooden ceiling shows another structural approach. Carved Gothic portals (哥德式門楣雕刻) and stained glass show detailed craft, and the amber collection (琥珀) recalls the Baltic trade that made the Order rich. Heavily damaged in 1945, the castle has been restored over decades. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a taxi driver, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 索波特與格丁尼亞
stations.en: Sopot & Gdynia: Resort and Modernist Port
stations.zhText: 格但斯克灣上相鄰的兩座城鎮，呈現兩種海濱想像。索波特是歷史悠久的度假地：1900 年前後的別墅與公寓有塔樓、凸窗與裝飾木作，還有哥德復興式磚造教堂和彩色立面的行人主街。歪歪屋（2004）把立面格線扭曲成表現性的商業地標；超過 500 公尺長的木棧橋把散步變成海上的漫遊。隔壁的格丁尼亞是兩次大戰之間幾乎從零建起的波蘭新港，市中心是少見的戰間期現代主義建築群：圓角、水平帶窗與舷窗的流線型建築說著船的語言，波莫熱號帆船就停在附近，博物館公寓則展示現代主義的居家設計。
stations.enText: Two neighbouring towns on the Gulf of Gdańsk show two ideas of the seaside. Sopot (索波特) is a historic resort: villas and tenements of around 1900 with towers, bay windows and decorative woodwork, a Gothic Revival (哥德復興式) brick church, and a pedestrian main street lined with colourful façades. Its Crooked House (歪歪屋, 2004) warps a façade grid into an expressive commercial landmark (表現性設計), and the wooden pier (棧橋), over 500 metres long, turns a walk into a promenade over the sea. Next door, Gdynia (格丁尼亞) was built almost from scratch between the wars as Poland's new port, and its centre is a rare ensemble of interwar Modernism (兩次大戰間現代主義). Streamline (流線型現代主義) buildings with rounded corners, ribbon windows (水平帶窗) and porthole windows (舷窗) speak the language of ships, the tall ship Dar Pomorza (波莫熱號帆船) is moored nearby, and a museum apartment shows Modernist domestic design (居家設計). Leisure and modernity sit side by side along one coast. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from a young local and a café host, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 海爾半島、西盤半島與瓦維爾城堡
stations.zhText: 這幾天從波羅的海岸走到克拉科夫的王室核心。海爾半島是長約 35 公里的沙嘴，結合運作中的漁港、漁網與小船構成的風土地景、被松林吞沒的戰時碉堡，以及八角形磚造燈塔。1939 年 9 月 1 日二戰在西盤半島開打，殘破的營房與彈痕累累的牆被保留為紀念地景，上方是 1966 年的海岸守軍紀念碑。格但斯克莫特瓦河畔穀倉島上的新建築重新詮釋舊穀倉形式，是文脈設計的例子。克拉科夫的瓦維爾城堡把義大利文藝復興帶到阿爾卑斯以北：拱廊中庭、雕刻方格天花，以及貝雷奇設計的鍍金齊格蒙特禮拜堂。地景、記憶與王室贊助，各自塑造出不同的場所。
stations.enText: These days travel from the Baltic coast to the royal heart of Kraków. The Hel Peninsula (海爾半島), a sandspit (沙嘴) about 35 kilometres long, combines a working fishing harbour, a vernacular landscape (風土地景) of nets and boats, wartime bunkers (軍事建築) absorbed by pine forest, and an octagonal brick lighthouse (燈塔). At Westerplatte (西盤半島), where the Second World War began on 1 September 1939, ruined barracks and bullet-marked walls are preserved as a memorial landscape (紀念地景), crowned by the 1966 Monument to the Coast Defenders. On the Motława (莫特瓦河) waterfront in Gdańsk, new buildings on Granary Island (穀倉島) reinterpret old granary forms, an example of contextual design (文脈設計). In Kraków, Wawel Royal Castle (瓦維爾城堡) shows Italian Renaissance (義大利文藝復興) architecture north of the Alps: an arcaded courtyard (拱廊中庭), carved coffered ceilings (方格天花) and Berrecci's gilded Sigismund Chapel (齊格蒙特禮拜堂). Landscape, memory and royal patronage (王室贊助) each shape a different kind of place. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from our guide and local students at Westerplatte, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 克拉科夫老城、卡齊米日與植物園
stations.en: Kraków: Old Town, Manggha, Kazimierz & Garden
stations.zhText: 在克拉科夫的幾天，從中世紀廣場一路走到日本設計、民俗藝術和植物形態。中央廣場的紡織會館有文藝復興式女兒牆，聖母聖殿是一高一低雙塔的磚造哥德式教堂。磯崎新設計的曼加日本藝術科技博物館（1994）有波浪屋頂，展出產品設計與日文字型設計。卡齊米日的伯納特克橋上懸著平衡特技人雕塑；民族誌博物館展出剪紙、民俗彩繪與列入世界遺產的克拉科夫耶誕馬槽。1783 年創立的雅蓋隆大學植物園溫室，則是一座自然形態的圖書館。
stations.enText: Several days in Kraków (克拉科夫) move from medieval square to Japanese design, folk art and plant form. The Main Square (中央廣場) centres on the Cloth Hall (紡織會館) with its Renaissance parapet attic (女兒牆) and St Mary's Basilica (聖母聖殿), a Brick Gothic (磚造哥德式) church with unequal towers and Veit Stoss's altarpiece. Arata Isozaki's Manggha Museum (曼加日本藝術科技博物館, 1994) has a wave-like roof (波浪屋頂) and showed product design (產品設計) and Japanese typography (日文字型設計). In Kazimierz (卡齊米日), balancing acrobat sculptures (特技人雕塑) hang from the Bernatek footbridge, and the Ethnographic Museum (民族誌博物館) presents folk art (民俗藝術), paper cut-outs (剪紙) and the UNESCO-listed Kraków Nativity scenes (克拉科夫耶誕馬槽). The Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden (雅蓋隆大學植物園), founded in 1783, adds glasshouses (溫室) and a library of natural form (自然形態), the source of much biomorphic design (生物形態設計). City, craft and nature appear here as one continuous design education. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from locals in Kraków, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.

stations.zh: 維利奇卡鹽礦與奧斯威辛紀念館
stations.zhText: 克拉科夫附近的兩處世界遺產，因日期相近放在一起，而非主題相同。維利奇卡鹽礦是由廳室與禮拜堂組成的地下世界，礦工把岩鹽雕成雕像與浮雕，並以木框支撐與絞盤構成坑道；有鹽製吊燈與《最後的晚餐》浮雕的聖金加禮拜堂，示範「減法」的工藝。奧斯威辛—比克瑙是納粹德國的集中營與滅絕營，放在這裡不是當作設計景點，而是因為它提出紀念設計與保存的根本問題：受難者的遺物、囚犯照片、比克瑙的鐵道大門與一排排營房都被保留為證據。場所真實性、克制的展示、以真實物件取代重建，提醒設計者思考什麼是永遠不該被裝飾的。
stations.enText: Two UNESCO World Heritage Sites near Kraków are grouped here by date, not by theme. The Wieliczka Salt Mine (維利奇卡鹽礦) is an underground world of chambers and chapels where miners carved rock salt (岩鹽) into sculpture and reliefs and used timber cribbing (木框支撐) and winding gear (絞盤); the Chapel of St Kinga (聖金加禮拜堂), with its salt chandeliers and Last Supper (最後的晚餐) relief, shows craft by subtraction. Auschwitz-Birkenau (奧斯威辛—比克瑙), the German Nazi concentration and extermination camp, is included not as a design attraction but because it raises essential questions of memorial design (紀念設計) and preservation (保存). The victims' own belongings, prisoner photographs, the railway gate at Birkenau and the rows of barracks are kept as evidence. Authenticity of place (場所真實性), restraint in display and real objects instead of reconstruction are its central principles, and they ask designers to consider what should never be decorated.

stations.zh: 新胡塔與華沙天際線
stations.en: From Nowa Huta to Warsaw: Socialist City & Skyline
stations.zhText: 最後幾天比較意識形態、記憶與資本如何塑造城市。克拉科夫的新胡塔自 1949 年規劃為社會主義模範城，有放射狀規劃與社會寫實主義的拱廊街廓；以河石包覆、外形如船的現代主義「主之方舟」教堂，是居民長期爭取才建成的。柯斯丘什科土丘（1820–1823）是地景紀念物，後來被紅磚堡壘環繞。華沙的文化科學宮（1952–1955）是階梯式的史達林風格高樓，女兒牆引用波蘭文藝復興的造型；福斯特事務所的 Varso 塔（2022）是歐盟最高建築，從上面看城市就像一張都市計畫圖。重建的舊城裡，巴洛克祭壇、哥德式網狀拱頂、齊格蒙特圓柱與刮畫立面，完成一條由權力、商業與信仰組成的天際線。
stations.enText: The final days compare how ideology, memory and money shape cities. In Kraków, Nowa Huta (新胡塔), planned from 1949 as a model socialist town, has a radial plan (放射狀規劃) and arcaded blocks (拱廊) in the Socialist Realist (社會寫實主義) style; the Ark of the Lord (方舟教堂), a ship-shaped Modernist church clad in river stones, was won by residents' long campaign. The Kościuszko Mound (柯斯丘什科土丘, 1820–1823) is a landscape monument (地景紀念物) later wrapped in a red-brick fortress (紅磚堡壘). In Warsaw (華沙), the Palace of Culture and Science (文化科學宮, 1952–1955) is a stepped Stalinist tower whose parapets quote Polish Renaissance attics, while Foster + Partners' Varso Tower (Varso 塔, 2022), the tallest building in the European Union, offers a view that reads like a city plan (都市計畫). In the rebuilt Old Town (舊城), Baroque altars, Gothic net vaulting (網狀拱頂), Sigismund's Column and sgraffito (刮畫) façades complete a skyline (天際線) of power, commerce and faith. Meeting local people (與在地人互動), from taxi drivers and market vendors, was part of the journey too: travel is also learning from people, not only from buildings.
